name: jira_add_attachment
description: Attach a local file to a Jira issue.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the file to attach

name: jira_add_comment
description: Add a comment to a Jira issue. Supports standard Markdown, automatically converted to ADF.

visibility.description: Restrict who can read the comment, e.g. { "type": "role", "value": "Administrators" }. Omit to leave it visible to everyone who can see the issue.

internal.description: Jira Service Management only: post as an internal note that the customer cannot see.

name: jira_add_issues_to_epic
description: Link one or more issues to an epic. Uses Agile API bulk move.

issueKeys.description: Array of issue keys to attach to the epic

name: jira_add_remote_link
description: Attach a web link to an issue, e.g. the pull request that implements it or the Confluence page that specifies it.

url.description: Link target. Must be http or https.

title.description: Link text shown on the issue

relationship.description: How the link relates, e.g. "implemented by", "documented in"

globalId.description: Stable identifier. Posting the same globalId again updates that link instead of adding a duplicate.

name: jira_add_watcher
description: Subscribe a user to watch an issue (receive notifications on changes).

accountId.description: Atlassian accountId of the user to add as watcher. Omit to add the authenticated user.

name: jira_add_worklog
description: Add a worklog entry (time tracking). `timeSpent` uses Jira units: w (week), d (day, 8h by default), h (hour), m (minute). `started` must be ISO 8601 with millisecond and timezone offset, e.g. "2024-01-15T09:00:00.000+0000" (NOT a Z-terminated ISO). If omitted, server uses now.

timeSpent.description: Jira-style duration. Examples: "2h 30m", "1d", "45m", "3w 2d". Max units w/d/h/m.

started.description: Start time as ISO 8601 with millis and offset, e.g. "2024-01-15T09:00:00.000+0000". Defaults to now.

name: jira_assign_issue
description: Assign or unassign a user. Jira uses accountId (not email or username). To find accountId: call jira_search_users by name/email, or jira_get_myself for the current user. Pass null accountId to unassign.

accountId.description: Atlassian accountId of the assignee (opaque string like "5b10a2844c20165700ede21g"), or null to unassign. Get via jira_search_users or jira_get_myself.

name: jira_bulk_create_issues
description: Create multiple Jira issues at once. Descriptions support Markdown, automatically converted to ADF.

issueType.description: Issue type name or id (Story, Task, Bug, etc.). Names are resolved to ids.

priority.description: Priority id (preferred) or name. Names are localized on non-English instances and only the canonical English name works — pass the id from jira_get_priorities or jira_get_create_fields. A localized name is matched against the allowed values and converted to an id automatically.

parent.description: Parent issue key (epic or parent task).

versions.description: Affects versions, by name or numeric id (ids are used verbatim). Required on many Bug screens. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

fixVersions.description: Fix versions, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

components.description: Components, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_components.

assignee.description: Assignee accountId (not email). Resolve via jira_search_users or jira_get_myself.

reporter.description: Reporter accountId (not email). Requires the Modify Reporter permission.

customFields.description: Custom field values keyed by field ID (customfield_NNNNN). Use the shape the field expects: single-select { "id": "10001" } or { "value": "X" }; multi-select [ { "id": "10001" } ]; user { "accountId": "..." }; text "string". Rich-text (schema.type "doc") fields accept a plain Markdown string and are converted to ADF automatically. Call jira_get_create_fields for ids and allowed values.

customFieldsMarkdown.description: Rich-text custom fields keyed by field ID, values as Markdown strings converted to ADF. Use when the field type is "doc" and you want the conversion to be explicit.

name: jira_bulk_transition_issues
description: Apply the same status transition to multiple issues. Iterates client-side; failures are collected per issue and returned. status is matched against each transition target status first, then transition names, case-insensitively — so "In Progress" works even where the transition is called "Start work". Use transitionFields when the transition screen requires input.

issueKeys.description: Array of issue keys to transition

transitionId.description: Exact transition ID from jira_list_transitions. Takes precedence over status.

status.description: Target status name (e.g. "In Progress") or transition name. Resolved per issue.

transitionName.description: Deprecated alias for status, kept for compatibility.

transitionFields.description: Fields required by the transition screen, keyed by field ID. Call jira_list_transitions with includeFields to see what a transition requires.

comment.description: Optional comment added during the transition (Markdown)

name: jira_bulk_update_issues
description: Apply the same field changes to many issues. Iterates client-side with a per-issue result, because Jira has no stable bulk edit endpoint. Use addLabels/removeLabels to adjust labels without destroying the ones already there; the labels argument replaces the whole list on every issue.

addLabels.description: Labels to add, leaving existing ones alone

removeLabels.description: Labels to remove, leaving the rest alone

priority.description: Priority id (preferred) or name. Names are localized on non-English instances and only the canonical English name works — pass the id from jira_get_priorities or jira_get_create_fields. A localized name is matched against the allowed values and converted to an id automatically.

parent.description: New parent issue key for every listed issue

versions.description: Affects versions, by name or numeric id (ids are used verbatim). Required on many Bug screens. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

fixVersions.description: Fix versions, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

components.description: Components, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_components.

assignee.description: Assignee accountId (not email). Resolve via jira_search_users or jira_get_myself.

reporter.description: Reporter accountId (not email). Requires the Modify Reporter permission.

customFields.description: Custom field values keyed by field ID (customfield_NNNNN). Use the shape the field expects: single-select { "id": "10001" } or { "value": "X" }; multi-select [ { "id": "10001" } ]; user { "accountId": "..." }; text "string". Rich-text (schema.type "doc") fields accept a plain Markdown string and are converted to ADF automatically. Call jira_get_create_fields for ids and allowed values.

customFieldsMarkdown.description: Rich-text custom fields keyed by field ID, values as Markdown strings converted to ADF. Use when the field type is "doc" and you want the conversion to be explicit.

name: jira_clone_issue
description: Clone an existing Jira issue with a new summary. Copies issue type, description, labels, priority, story points, components and versions from the source. Custom fields are NOT copied — supply any the target screen requires via customFields. Any field passed explicitly overrides the copied value.

summary.description: Summary for the cloned issue (defaults to "Clone of <original>")

projectKey.description: Target project key (defaults to same project as source)

priority.description: Priority id (preferred) or name. Names are localized on non-English instances and only the canonical English name works — pass the id from jira_get_priorities or jira_get_create_fields. A localized name is matched against the allowed values and converted to an id automatically.

storyPoints.description: Story points estimate (0-1000). Overrides the copied value.

parent.description: Parent issue key (epic or parent task).

versions.description: Affects versions, by name or numeric id (ids are used verbatim). Required on many Bug screens. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

fixVersions.description: Fix versions, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

components.description: Components, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_components.

assignee.description: Assignee accountId (not email). Resolve via jira_search_users or jira_get_myself.

reporter.description: Reporter accountId (not email). Requires the Modify Reporter permission.

customFields.description: Custom field values keyed by field ID (customfield_NNNNN). Use the shape the field expects: single-select { "id": "10001" } or { "value": "X" }; multi-select [ { "id": "10001" } ]; user { "accountId": "..." }; text "string". Rich-text (schema.type "doc") fields accept a plain Markdown string and are converted to ADF automatically. Call jira_get_create_fields for ids and allowed values.

customFieldsMarkdown.description: Rich-text custom fields keyed by field ID, values as Markdown strings converted to ADF. Use when the field type is "doc" and you want the conversion to be explicit.

name: jira_create_component
description: Create a project component. Components are the values the components field accepts on create and update.

assigneeType.description: Default assignee rule for issues in this component

name: jira_create_epic
description: Create a new epic. Convenience wrapper that sets issueType to Epic.

epicName.description: Short name for classic (company-managed) projects. Sent only when the create screen actually has the Epic Name field.

priority.description: Priority id (preferred) or name. Names are localized on non-English instances and only the canonical English name works — pass the id from jira_get_priorities or jira_get_create_fields. A localized name is matched against the allowed values and converted to an id automatically.

versions.description: Affects versions, by name or numeric id (ids are used verbatim). Required on many Bug screens. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

fixVersions.description: Fix versions, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

components.description: Components, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_components.

assignee.description: Assignee accountId (not email). Resolve via jira_search_users or jira_get_myself.

reporter.description: Reporter accountId (not email). Requires the Modify Reporter permission.

customFields.description: Custom field values keyed by field ID (customfield_NNNNN). Use the shape the field expects: single-select { "id": "10001" } or { "value": "X" }; multi-select [ { "id": "10001" } ]; user { "accountId": "..." }; text "string". Rich-text (schema.type "doc") fields accept a plain Markdown string and are converted to ADF automatically. Call jira_get_create_fields for ids and allowed values.

customFieldsMarkdown.description: Rich-text custom fields keyed by field ID, values as Markdown strings converted to ADF. Use when the field type is "doc" and you want the conversion to be explicit.

dryRun.description: When true, validate against the create screen and return what is missing without creating the epic.

name: jira_create_issue
description: Create a new Jira issue. Description supports Markdown (auto-converted to ADF). To create an Epic use jira_create_epic. Call jira_get_create_fields(projectKey, issueType) first when the screen is unknown — it returns every field with required, type and allowedValues, which removes the guesswork (Bug screens commonly require Affects versions and other mandatory fields). Optional fields are only sent when provided, so nothing is rejected for not being on the screen. On a 400 the response carries missingRequired and allowedValues. Set dryRun to validate the payload without creating anything.

description.description: Issue description in Markdown. Use [KEY](url) for clickable issue links.

issueType.description: Issue type name or id. Names are localized on non-English instances; a name is resolved to an id automatically. Call jira_get_issue_types for the definitive list.

priority.description: Priority id (preferred) or name. Names are localized on non-English instances and only the canonical English name works — pass the id from jira_get_priorities or jira_get_create_fields. A localized name is matched against the allowed values and converted to an id automatically.

parent.description: Parent issue key — the epic for a story, or the parent for a subtask (e.g. "PROJ-12").

versions.description: Affects versions, by name or numeric id (ids are used verbatim). Required on many Bug screens. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

fixVersions.description: Fix versions, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

components.description: Components, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_components.

assignee.description: Assignee accountId (not email). Resolve via jira_search_users or jira_get_myself.

reporter.description: Reporter accountId (not email). Requires the Modify Reporter permission.

customFields.description: Custom field values keyed by field ID (customfield_NNNNN). Use the shape the field expects: single-select { "id": "10001" } or { "value": "X" }; multi-select [ { "id": "10001" } ]; user { "accountId": "..." }; text "string". Rich-text (schema.type "doc") fields accept a plain Markdown string and are converted to ADF automatically. Call jira_get_create_fields for ids and allowed values.

customFieldsMarkdown.description: Rich-text custom fields keyed by field ID, values as Markdown strings converted to ADF. Use when the field type is "doc" and you want the conversion to be explicit.

dryRun.description: When true, validate the payload against the create screen and return missingRequired / invalidValues / fieldsNotOnScreen without creating the issue.

name: jira_create_sprint
description: Create a sprint on a Scrum board. A new sprint starts in the "future" state; use jira_update_sprint with state "active" to start it. Board ids come from jira_list_boards.

boardId.description: Board the sprint belongs to (use jira_list_boards)

name: jira_create_subtask
description: Create a subtask under a parent issue. Description supports standard Markdown, automatically converted to ADF. The subtask issue type is discovered from the project (handles "Sub-task" vs "Subtask" and localized names) unless issueType is given.

description.description: Subtask description in Markdown. Use [KEY](url) for clickable issue links.

issueType.description: Subtask issue type name or id. Defaults to the project's subtask type.

priority.description: Priority id (preferred) or name. Names are localized on non-English instances and only the canonical English name works — pass the id from jira_get_priorities or jira_get_create_fields. A localized name is matched against the allowed values and converted to an id automatically.

versions.description: Affects versions, by name or numeric id (ids are used verbatim). Required on many Bug screens. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

fixVersions.description: Fix versions, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

components.description: Components, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_components.

assignee.description: Assignee accountId (not email). Resolve via jira_search_users or jira_get_myself.

reporter.description: Reporter accountId (not email). Requires the Modify Reporter permission.

customFields.description: Custom field values keyed by field ID (customfield_NNNNN). Use the shape the field expects: single-select { "id": "10001" } or { "value": "X" }; multi-select [ { "id": "10001" } ]; user { "accountId": "..." }; text "string". Rich-text (schema.type "doc") fields accept a plain Markdown string and are converted to ADF automatically. Call jira_get_create_fields for ids and allowed values.

customFieldsMarkdown.description: Rich-text custom fields keyed by field ID, values as Markdown strings converted to ADF. Use when the field type is "doc" and you want the conversion to be explicit.

dryRun.description: When true, validate against the create screen and return what is missing without creating the subtask.

name: jira_create_version
description: Create a project version (release). Versions are what fixVersions and affects versions point at, so create one here instead of sending the user to the Jira UI.

name: jira_delete_attachment
description: Permanently delete an attachment. Attachment ids come from jira_get_attachments. This cannot be undone — confirm with the user first.

name: jira_delete_comment
description: Delete a comment from a Jira issue.

commentId.description: Comment ID (use jira_get_comments to find it)

name: jira_delete_component
description: Permanently delete a project component. Pass moveIssuesTo to reassign its issues to another component, otherwise they simply lose it. This cannot be undone -- confirm with the user first.

moveIssuesTo.description: Component ID to move issues to. Omit to clear the field on those issues.

name: jira_delete_issue
description: Permanently delete a Jira issue. This cannot be undone and there is no trash to restore from — confirm with the user before calling it. An issue that has subtasks is rejected unless deleteSubtasks is set, which deletes them too.

deleteSubtasks.description: Also delete every subtask of this issue. Without it, Jira refuses to delete an issue that has subtasks.

name: jira_delete_issue_link
description: Remove a link between two issues. The linkId comes from the links array returned by jira_get_issue, not from the issue keys.

name: jira_delete_remote_link
description: Remove a web link from an issue. Link ids come from jira_get_remote_links.

name: jira_delete_sprint
description: Permanently delete a sprint. Issues in it are moved to the backlog. This cannot be undone -- confirm with the user first.

name: jira_delete_version
description: Permanently delete a project version. Issues referencing it keep their other fields, but lose this version unless you pass a replacement. This cannot be undone -- confirm with the user first.

moveFixIssuesTo.description: Version ID to move fixVersion references to. Omit to clear them.

moveAffectedIssuesTo.description: Version ID to move affects-version references to. Omit to clear them.

name: jira_delete_worklog
description: Delete a worklog entry from a Jira issue. Permanent.

worklogId.description: Worklog ID (use jira_get_worklogs to find it)

name: jira_download_attachment
description: Download an attachment from Jira to a local file. Destination path must be within cwd or user home.

savePath.description: Absolute local path where the file will be written

name: jira_get_attachments
description: Get list of attachments on a Jira issue.

name: jira_get_board_epics
description: List epics on a Scrum/Kanban board, optionally filtered by done status.

done.description: Filter: "true" for done epics, "false" for active, omit for all

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first item to return. Use it with the returned startAt/total/hasMore to page beyond the first batch.

name: jira_get_changelog
description: Get the change history of a Jira issue (who changed what and when).

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first item to return. Use it with the returned startAt/total/hasMore to page beyond the first batch.

name: jira_get_comments
description: Get comments from a Jira issue.

orderBy.description: Order by created date: "created" (oldest first) or "-created" (newest first)

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first item to return. Use it with the returned startAt/total/hasMore to page beyond the first batch.

name: jira_get_create_fields
description: Get the create screen definition for one issue type: every field with fieldId, name, required, type and allowedValues, plus a requiredFields shortlist. This is the second createmeta step (jira_get_issue_types is the first) and it is what tells you which fields are mandatory and which values they accept. Call it before jira_create_issue on an unfamiliar project or issue type instead of guessing.

issueType.description: Issue type name or id (e.g. "Bug" or "10004"). Names are matched case-insensitively and work with localized names.

name: jira_get_edit_fields
description: Get the edit screen for one existing issue: every field you may change, with required flags, types and allowed values. This is the update-time mirror of jira_get_create_fields, and the way to find out why a field is rejected on jira_update_issue.

name: jira_get_epic
description: Get epic details via Agile API (name, summary, color, done status).

fields.description: Exact field IDs to return per issue, e.g. ["summary", "customfield_10122"] or ["*all"]. When set, each item returns a raw fields map instead of the default shape.

includeCustomFields.description: Add a customFields map (id -> { name, type, value }) to every issue. Rich-text fields render as Markdown. Requests all fields, so prefer an explicit fields list on large result sets.

name: jira_get_epic_issues
description: Get all child issues linked to an epic.

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first item to return. Use it with the returned startAt/total/hasMore to page beyond the first batch.

fields.description: Exact field IDs to return per issue, e.g. ["summary", "customfield_10122"] or ["*all"]. When set, each item returns a raw fields map instead of the default shape.

includeCustomFields.description: Add a customFields map (id -> { name, type, value }) to every issue. Rich-text fields render as Markdown. Requests all fields, so prefer an explicit fields list on large result sets.

name: jira_get_fields
description: Get all available Jira fields. Useful for finding custom field IDs.

name: jira_get_filter
description: Get a saved filter by ID, including its JQL, description, and owner.

name: jira_get_issue
description: Get details of a Jira issue. The default response includes status, resolution, assignee, priority, labels, story points, parent, components, versions, fixVersions, dueDate and timetracking. Set includeCustomFields to also get every populated custom field with its human-readable name (rich-text ones rendered as Markdown), or pass fields to select an exact set. Set includeImages to return embedded/attached images inline.

fields.description: Exact field IDs to return (passed to the Jira ?fields= parameter), e.g. ["summary", "versions", "customfield_10122"] or ["*all"]. When set, the response returns a raw fields map instead of the default shape.

includeCustomFields.description: When true, add a customFields map of every populated customfield_NNNNN with { name, type, value }. Rich-text (doc) fields are converted to Markdown.

includeImages.description: When true, return up to 10 image attachments (image/*, each <=5MB) as inline images, embedded-in-description ones first. Default false.

name: jira_get_issue_types
description: Get all available issue types for a project. Names are rendered in the Jira account language — prefer the id when passing a type on. For the fields a given type requires, call jira_get_create_fields.

name: jira_get_link_types
description: Get all available issue link types.

name: jira_get_my_permissions
description: Check what the authenticated user is allowed to do, optionally scoped to a project or an issue. Call it before a bulk operation to fail early with a clear reason instead of collecting permission errors issue by issue.

projectKey.description: Scope the check to a project

issueKey.description: Scope the check to a single issue

permissions.description: Permission keys to check, e.g. ["EDIT_ISSUES", "DELETE_ISSUES"]. Defaults to the common project permissions.

name: jira_get_myself
description: Get the authenticated user (accountId, displayName, email, timezone, locale). Useful to know who the MCP server is acting as.

name: jira_get_priorities
description: Get all available issue priorities. Returns id first: the name is rendered in the Jira account language and Jira only accepts the canonical English name or the id on create/update, so pass the id.

name: jira_get_project_components
description: Get components of a Jira project.

name: jira_get_project_info
description: Get project information

name: jira_get_project_statuses
description: Get every status available per issue type in a project, with its status category. Use it to write correct JQL and to know which statuses exist before trying to transition to one.

name: jira_get_project_versions
description: Get versions (releases) of a Jira project.

name: jira_get_remote_links
description: List web links attached to an issue — pull requests, Confluence pages, dashboards, anything outside Jira. These are separate from issue-to-issue links, which jira_get_issue returns.

name: jira_get_sprint
description: Get details of a sprint including all issues in it.

sprintId.description: Sprint ID (use jira_list_sprints to find it)

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first item to return. Use it with the returned startAt/total/hasMore to page beyond the first batch.

fields.description: Exact field IDs to return per issue, e.g. ["summary", "customfield_10122"] or ["*all"]. When set, each item returns a raw fields map instead of the default shape.

includeCustomFields.description: Add a customFields map (id -> { name, type, value }) to every issue. Rich-text fields render as Markdown. Requests all fields, so prefer an explicit fields list on large result sets.

name: jira_get_user_issues
description: Get all issues assigned to a specific user.

accountId.description: Atlassian account ID of the user

projectKey.description: Filter by project key (defaults to configured JIRA_PROJECT_KEY)

fields.description: Exact field IDs to return per issue, e.g. ["summary", "customfield_10122"] or ["*all"]. When set, each item returns a raw fields map instead of the default shape.

includeCustomFields.description: Add a customFields map (id -> { name, type, value }) to every issue. Rich-text fields render as Markdown. Requests all fields, so prefer an explicit fields list on large result sets.

name: jira_get_watchers
description: List all watchers on an issue.

name: jira_get_worklogs
description: Get worklog entries from a Jira issue.

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first item to return. Use it with the returned startAt/total/hasMore to page beyond the first batch.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of worklog entries (1-100). Omit to let Jira return every entry.

name: jira_link_issues
description: Create a link between two issues. The inward side uses the linkType.inward phrasing ("is blocked by", "duplicates"), the outward side uses linkType.outward ("blocks", "is duplicated by"). If unsure which linkType names exist in this instance, call jira_get_link_types. Call sequentially (2-3 at a time) to avoid permission prompt storms in Claude Code.

inwardIssue.description: Issue key on the inward side (the one that "is blocked by" / "duplicates" the other)

outwardIssue.description: Issue key on the outward side (the one that "blocks" / "is duplicated by" the inward one)

linkType.description: Link type name. Common: Relates, Blocks, Duplicate, Cloners. Call jira_get_link_types for instance-specific list.

name: jira_list_boards
description: List all Scrum/Kanban boards.

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first item to return. Use it with the returned startAt/total/hasMore to page beyond the first batch.

name: jira_list_epics
description: List all epics in a project via JQL (issuetype = Epic).

fields.description: Exact field IDs to return per epic, e.g. ["summary", "customfield_10122"] or ["*all"]. When set, each item returns a raw fields map instead of the default shape.

includeCustomFields.description: Add a customFields map (id -> { name, type, value }) to every epic. Rich-text fields render as Markdown.

name: jira_list_filters
description: Search saved Jira filters (by name, owner). Useful to retrieve team-defined JQL queries.

filterName.description: Substring to match in filter name

accountId.description: Filter owner accountId (defaults to authenticated user if both name and accountId omitted)

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first item to return. Use it with the returned startAt/total/hasMore to page beyond the first batch.

name: jira_list_labels
description: List labels that already exist in this Jira instance. Use it to reuse an existing label instead of inventing a near-duplicate.

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first label to return

name: jira_list_projects
description: List all accessible Jira projects.

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first item to return. Use it with the returned startAt/total/hasMore to page beyond the first batch.

name: jira_list_sprints
description: List sprints for a board.

boardId.description: Board ID (use jira_list_boards to find it)

state.description: Filter by state: active, future, closed

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first item to return. Use it with the returned startAt/total/hasMore to page beyond the first batch.

name: jira_list_transitions
description: Get available status transitions for a Jira issue. Each entry has the transition id and name plus the target status under "to" — a workflow can name a transition "Start work" while its target status is "In Progress". Set includeFields to also get the fields each transition screen accepts, with required flags and allowed values, for passing via jira_update_issue transitionFields.

includeFields.description: When true, expand each transition with its screen fields (fieldId, name, required, type, allowedValues) and a requiredFields shortlist.

name: jira_move_to_backlog
description: Move issues out of their sprint and back to the backlog. The inverse of jira_move_to_sprint.

issueKeys.description: Issue keys to move to the backlog

name: jira_move_to_sprint
description: Move one or more issues to a sprint.

sprintId.description: Sprint ID (use jira_list_sprints to find it)

issueKeys.description: Array of issue keys to move (e.g., ["PROJ-1", "PROJ-2"])

name: jira_rank_issues
description: Reorder issues in the backlog or on a board by placing them before or after a reference issue. This is what changes the order sprint planning reads as priority.

issueKeys.description: Issues to move (max 50), kept in the given order

rankBeforeIssue.description: Place them immediately above this issue

rankAfterIssue.description: Place them immediately below this issue

name: jira_remove_issue_from_epic
description: Remove issues from their current epic (unlink).

issueKeys.description: Array of issue keys to detach from their epic

name: jira_remove_watcher
description: Unsubscribe a user from watching an issue.

name: jira_search_by_filter
description: Execute a saved filter's JQL and return matching issues.

fields.description: Exact field IDs to return per issue, e.g. ["summary", "customfield_10122"] or ["*all"]. When set, each item returns a raw fields map instead of the default shape.

includeCustomFields.description: Add a customFields map (id -> { name, type, value }) to every issue. Rich-text fields render as Markdown. Requests all fields, so prefer an explicit fields list on large result sets.

name: jira_search_issues
description: Search for Jira issues using JQL. Uses token-based pagination — pass nextPageToken from previous response to get next page.

nextPageToken.description: Pagination token from previous search response

fields.description: Exact field IDs to return per issue, e.g. ["summary", "customfield_10122"] or ["*all"]. When set, each item returns a raw fields map instead of the default shape.

includeCustomFields.description: Add a customFields map (id -> { name, type, value }) to every issue. Rich-text fields render as Markdown. Requests all fields, so prefer an explicit fields list on large result sets.

name: jira_search_users
description: Search for Jira users by name or email. Returns accountId needed for jira_assign_issue.

query.description: Search query (matches display name and email prefix)

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first item to return. Use it with the returned startAt/total/hasMore to page beyond the first batch.

name: jira_update_comment
description: Update an existing comment on a Jira issue. Supports standard Markdown, automatically converted to ADF.

commentId.description: Comment ID (use jira_get_comments to find it)

visibility.description: Restrict who can read the comment, e.g. { "type": "role", "value": "Administrators" }. Omit to leave it visible to everyone who can see the issue.

internal.description: Jira Service Management only: post as an internal note that the customer cannot see.

name: jira_update_component
description: Update a project component. Component ids come from jira_get_project_components.

name: jira_update_issue
description: Update fields and/or status of an issue. status is matched against the target status of each available transition first (so "In Progress" works even when the transition is named "Start work"), then against transition names, case-insensitively. Use transitionId for an exact transition and transitionFields when the transition screen requires input (e.g. an estimate) — jira_list_transitions with includeFields lists what each one needs. On a 400 the response carries missingRequired and allowedValues.

description.description: New description in Markdown. Use [KEY](url) for clickable issue links.

status.description: Target status name (e.g. "In Progress", "To Do") or transition name. Matched on the transition target status first, then the transition name, case-insensitively.

transitionId.description: Exact transition id from jira_list_transitions. Takes precedence over status.

transitionFields.description: Fields required by the transition screen, keyed by field ID (e.g. { "customfield_10016": 3, "resolution": { "id": "10000" } }). Call jira_list_transitions with includeFields to see what a transition requires.

priority.description: Priority id (preferred) or name. Names are localized on non-English instances and only the canonical English name works — pass the id from jira_get_priorities or jira_get_create_fields. A localized name is matched against the allowed values and converted to an id automatically.

parent.description: New parent issue key (epic or parent task).

versions.description: Affects versions, by name or numeric id (ids are used verbatim). Required on many Bug screens. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

fixVersions.description: Fix versions, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_versions.

components.description: Components, by name or numeric id. List them with jira_get_project_components.

assignee.description: Assignee accountId (not email). Resolve via jira_search_users or jira_get_myself.

reporter.description: Reporter accountId (not email). Requires the Modify Reporter permission.

customFields.description: Custom field values keyed by field ID (customfield_NNNNN). Use the shape the field expects: single-select { "id": "10001" } or { "value": "X" }; multi-select [ { "id": "10001" } ]; user { "accountId": "..." }; text "string". Rich-text (schema.type "doc") fields accept a plain Markdown string and are converted to ADF automatically. Call jira_get_create_fields for ids and allowed values.

customFieldsMarkdown.description: Rich-text custom fields keyed by field ID, values as Markdown strings converted to ADF. Use when the field type is "doc" and you want the conversion to be explicit.

name: jira_update_sprint
description: Update a sprint: rename it, set the goal or dates, or move it through the workflow with state ("future" -> "active" -> "closed"). Starting a sprint requires startDate and endDate to be set. Closing a sprint moves unfinished issues to the backlog in Jira, so confirm before setting state to "closed".

name: jira_update_version
description: Update a project version. Releasing a version is an update with released set to true (and usually a releaseDate), so there is no separate release tool. Version ids come from jira_get_project_versions.

released.description: Set true to release the version, false to unrelease it

name: jira_update_worklog
description: Update an existing worklog entry on a Jira issue. All fields except issueKey/worklogId are optional - omit to leave unchanged.

worklogId.description: Worklog ID (use jira_get_worklogs to find it)

timeSpent.description: New duration in Jira format ("2h 30m", "1d", "45m"). Optional.

started.description: New start time as ISO 8601 with millis and offset, e.g. "2024-01-15T09:00:00.000+0000". Optional.

name: jira_view_attachment
description: Fetch an image attachment and return it inline so the model can see it (no file written). Image attachments only (mimeType image/*), capped at 5MB. For non-images or larger files use jira_download_attachment. Get the attachmentId from jira_get_attachments.
